title: Display earnings/dividend dates, short interest, and insider transactions
description: Surface the newly-exposed earnings/dividend dates, short interest, and insider-transaction data (backend-market-data-extra-fields) on the stock detail page as a new panel. The earnings-date warning is the highest-value piece -- Elder's own rationale is explicit ('a nasty earnings surprise can do serious damage to your position... can jump straight past any stop level') -- so it should be visually prominent, not buried, when a position or a fresh BUY signal falls within the warning window. Handle the Stooq-fallback unavailability case explicitly (show 'unavailable' distinctly from 'checked, nothing found') rather than a silent blank. Per the project's established explanatory pattern (common/InfoBalloon, common/MetricHelp, metricHelpContent.ts, signalExplanation.ts, docs/tasks/frontend-stock-detail-metric-help.json), every new visual element this task adds must be explainable, not just displayed: a help affordance (reuse MetricHelp where it fits) that states what the metric/signal is, how it relates to Dr. Elder's methodology, and, where meaningful, an explanation of the CURRENT value shown -- not a static definition alone. Add an entry to metricHelpContent.ts's registry rather than inventing a parallel explanation mechanism.

checklist.step: Design the panel layout (earnings/dividend dates, short interest metrics, recent insider transactions) and the prominent earnings-warning treatment for positions/signals within the warning window.
Implement, handling the 'data unavailable on this provider path' case explicitly and distinctly from 'no data found.'

MetricHelp content explaining each field (what short-percent-of-float and days-to-cover mean and why a squeeze matters for a BUY; why 3+ insider buys/sells in a month is treated as meaningful but a single transaction isn't).
Tests + Storybook story; confirm 90% coverage gate holds.

decisions.decision: New `FundamentalDataPanel` (features/stocks/components/) is rendered directly below `SignalSummary` on `StockDetailPage`, ahead of `ScreensPanel`/`IndicatorsPanel`/`StockCharts` -- not appended after the existing panels, and not placed inside `SignalSummary` itself.
decisions.rationale: The task's own description calls the earnings-date warning 'the highest-value piece... should be visually prominent, not buried.' Appending the panel after ScreensPanel/IndicatorsPanel/StockCharts (the natural 'next new section' spot) would put the warning below several screenfuls of content on a typical viewport. Placing it directly under the signal/confidence summary keeps it above the fold on first load while staying a distinct component (not merged into SignalSummary itself, which already has its own single responsibility -- signal/confidence/profit-target -- and no knowledge of fundamentals data).

decisions.decision: The earnings-within-14-days warning banner is a plain MUI `Alert severity="warning"`, not a reuse of `components/common/RiskBreachBanner`.
decisions.rationale: RiskBreachBanner exists and is domain-agnostic (just an icon + message), so it was the first thing considered for reuse per the add-frontend-feature skill's step 2 duplication check. Its own doc comment and `theme.ts`'s `riskBreach` palette comment are explicit, though, that the color is deliberately reserved for the portfolio 2%/6% risk-rule breach specifically ('distinct from `signal.sell` so a risk breach banner never reads as "this is a SELL signal" -- it's a portfolio-level warning, not a per-stock signal'). Reusing that exact palette/component for an unrelated warning (an earnings date, not a risk-rule breach) would blur a distinction this codebase already established on purpose. A plain MUI `Alert` (already used elsewhere, e.g. `AddPositionDialog.tsx`) gives the same visual severity without repurposing a component whose color/semantics are pinned to a different meaning.

decisions.decision: The earnings-warning banner condition is `earnings_within_warning_days` alone (the backend's own 14-day flag), not narrowed to 'only when signal is a fresh BUY or a held position exists' as the task description's phrasing ('when a position or a fresh BUY signal falls within the warning window') might suggest.
decisions.rationale: This task is scoped to the stock detail page (area: frontend/pages/stocks) for an arbitrary looked-up ticker, which has no notion of 'is this currently a portfolio position' -- that's `features/portfolio/`'s domain, and wiring position awareness into this page would be meaningfully expanded scope beyond what the checklist asks for. The underlying risk Elder describes (an earnings gap defeating a protective stop) is just as real context for anyone considering, or currently holding, this ticker regardless of the page's own signal computation reaching BUY -- backend-market-data-extra-fields's own `earnings_within_warning_days` field is already signal-independent by design (it's computed from wall-clock `date.today()`, not gated on `signal`). Showing it unconditionally whenever the flag is true is the simpler, more broadly useful behavior and avoids duplicating signal-aware logic SignalSummary already owns.

decisions.decision: Insider transactions are rendered raw via `common/DataTable` (one row per filing, most-recent-first, exactly as the API returns them) with no client-side buy/sell classification or cluster detection -- `insiderTransactionsHelp`'s `interpretValue` states the filing count and Elder's 3+-within-a-month cluster threshold as an explanatory note, not a computed verdict.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the backend's own explicit decision (backend-market-data-extra-fields task) to expose insider transactions raw and defer cluster detection as a separate follow-up -- `transaction_text` is free-text yfinance prose ('Sale at price 220.00 - 225.00...') with no structured direction field to classify from without parsing it, which is exactly the scope that task's own decisions entry deferred. Computing a client-side cluster count here would both duplicate that deferred backend work in the wrong layer (detection logic belongs server-side, consistent with divergence/kangaroo-tail/support-resistance precedent) and risk a classification that disagrees with whatever the eventual backend cluster-detection task computes. The MetricHelp entry still explains the threshold Elder describes (ch. 37) so a reader knows what to look for themselves, satisfying the task's own checklist wording ('why 3+ insider buys/sells in a month is treated as meaningful but a single transaction isn't') without inventing unreviewed classification logic.

decisions.decision: `unavailable_reason === 'fallback_provider_active'` renders a distinct dashed-border card (same visual convention `ScreensPanel.tsx`'s Indicator Season card already established for 'informational, not the normal case') stating the cause explicitly, in place of the normal StatCard/short-interest/insider-table layout -- not a per-field '(unavailable)' annotation sprinkled through the normal layout.
decisions.rationale: The checklist calls for 'unavailable' to read distinctly from 'checked, nothing found,' and the backend's own `ExtendedDataOut.unavailable_reason` field description frames this as a structural, whole-object condition ('every field above is then null/empty, meaning not checked, unsupported by the active provider') rather than a per-field annotation -- every field is null/empty together in this state, so there is nothing meaningful left to show in the normal per-field layout anyway. A single explanatory card reusing the same dashed-border 'not a normal result' visual language already established elsewhere in this page is simpler and reads more clearly than threading an unavailable-vs-null distinction through six separate StatCard/table cells that would all say the same thing.

decisions.decision: `FundamentalDataPanel` treats `extendedData` as `ExtendedDataOut | null | undefined` and renders nothing (`return null`) when it's absent, even though the backend schema (`AnalysisResponse.extended_data`) is a non-optional, always-present field.
decisions.rationale: Several of `StockDetailPage.test.tsx`'s existing tests (the SELL/HOLD/season/lowercase-normalization cases, predating this task) hand-roll a partial `AnalysisResponse` JSON fixture via `HttpResponse.json({...})` that omits several optional-in-practice fields entirely, including (now) `extended_data` -- MSW doesn't validate the mocked response against the OpenAPI schema, so this compiles and runs fine, but would leave `extendedData` `undefined` at runtime for exactly those tests. Rather than rewriting every one of those pre-existing tests just to add a field this task's own scope doesn't require touching, the panel takes the same defensive posture `IndicatorsPanel.tsx`'s `formatValue` already documents toward a generated type it treats as optimistic, not a runtime guarantee -- gracefully rendering nothing rather than crashing. A real backend response always supplies the field, so this defensive branch is unreachable in production, only in this specific test-fixture-completeness gap.
